---
title: "How do I check whether consecutive observations are related?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I check whether consecutive observations are related?

## Steps to decide and solve

Put measurements in time order; inspect trends and repeated cycles; use the autocorrelation function and interpret each lag carefully.

## Worked example: Nile

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("Nile")
lags <- ru_apply("autocorrelation", data=d, x="flow", time="year")
stopifnot(inherits(lags,"acf"))
```

Autocorrelation compares a series with lagged versions of itself. A positive lag-one value can signal persistence, but trend, seasonality and irregular time spacing also affect its interpretation.

## Apply it to another question

```r
ru_apply("autocorrelation", data=your_data, x="numeric_column", time="date_column")
```

A raw ACF cannot establish stationarity; adjust the series or assess trend and changing variance where necessary.

Use `ru_plan("autocorrelation")` to inspect alternative routes when required information is absent or uncertain.
